source_refs.title: Live Caption: Caption media & calls on your device - Android Accessibility Help
source_refs.applicability: Android; device and language support varies by phone model
source_refs.verified_excerpt: With a single tap, Live Caption automatically captions speech on your device.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Android: Press a volume key to bring up the volume controls. Below the volume controls, tap 'More', then 'Live Caption', then 'Done'. On first use, connect to Wi-Fi to download the default language pack. If you don't see Live Caption, check with your phone manufacturer. If these steps don't work, search for 'Live Caption' in Settings and turn it on.

source_refs.title: Manage captions and translations in Chrome - Google Chrome Help
source_refs.section: Turning on Live Caption in Chrome, Windows or Mac
source_refs.applicability: Google Chrome on Windows or Mac; no Chrome version is stated
source_refs.verified_excerpt: All audio and captions are processed locally, are never stored, and never leave your device.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Chrome on Windows or Mac: Open Chrome. At the top right, select 'More', then 'Settings', then 'Accessibility'. Turn on 'Live Caption'.

source_refs.section: Turning on Live captions in Windows 11
source_refs.applicability: Windows 11, version 22H2 or later; live captions requires this version

source_refs.section: Turning on Live captions in Windows 11, first use
source_refs.verified_excerpt: When turned on the first time, live captions will ask for your consent to process voice data on your device
